details: Major central banks, including the US Federal Reserve, European Central Bank, and Bank of England, are signaling potential further interest rate increases. This comes as November's flash Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) data and Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price data are anticipated to provide crucial insights into economic activity and inflation. Persistent inflation and robust economic growth, as seen in South Korea's expected rate hike, are driving these hawkish stances.
title: Global Central Banks Hint at Further Rate Hikes

details: Ongoing geopolitical tensions, particularly in the Middle East, continue to influence global markets by keeping risks for commercial shipping and energy prices elevated. Conflicts, such as those impacting the Strait of Hormuz, can lead to abrupt price swings in energy markets. This situation contributes to inflationary pressures and fosters a "risk-off" sentiment among investors.
title: Middle East Tensions Sustain Elevated Energy & Shipping Risks

details: The cryptocurrency market is experiencing continued weakness, largely attributed to the increasing likelihood of a more restrictive Federal Reserve. Expectations of further interest rate hikes by the Fed into early 2027 have led to a noticeable decline in demand, with Bitcoin ETFs experiencing significant capital outflows. This trend reflects a broad deterioration in both retail and institutional investor confidence in speculative digital assets, as more stable alternative investments gain appeal.
title: Restrictive Fed Outlook Dampens Crypto Demand
